title: Micro‑Lab templates for LLM SDK patterns (Next.js / FastAPI / Go / CLI)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a small, focused set of micro‑lab templates that demonstrate idiomatic SDK usage across Next.js (edge + server), FastAPI, Go net/http, and a minimal CLI. These templates should surface best practices for: 1) streaming ergonomics (incremental render/resume), 2) retry/backoff policies (idempotency keys and per-language retry matrices), 3) token budget and abort semantics, and 4) developer experience for local debugging and CI smoke tests. The goal is not to be exhaustive but to provide compact, copy-pasteable examples teams can adapt quickly.
tasks: Design micro-lab scope and one-page README for each template
Implement Next.js example with edge function + server action demonstrating streaming + automatic cancellation
Build FastAPI example showing streaming ranges and server-side resume using KV cache stub
Create Go net/http example with middleware for retries, idempotency keys, and token budget enforcement
Add CLI example (Python) demonstrating retries, backoff visualization, and replayable logs
Write automated smoke tests that run examples in CI (Docker + minimal infra emulation)
Publish examples to repo examples/micro-labs and add quick links in SDK docs
acceptance_criteria: Each template has a one-file runnable example plus a README explaining trade-offs
Streaming examples support chunked rendering and a documented client pattern for resume/reconnect
Retry policies are implemented per SDK idiom (async/await for TS/Python, context + middleware for Go) and include idempotency key guidance
CI smoke tests run within 3m and validate correct header propagation, retry behavior, and basic latency SLOs
PRs include cross-language test harness and example CI job for downstream consumption
comments: 2025-02-14: Aisha Patel - Initial ticket created. Proposed scope focuses on ergonomics that repeatedly cause confusion in customer repo audits.

2025-02-17: Design review (María González) - Suggests clearer visuals in README showing client lifecycle (connect, partial render, resume, abort). Will add sequence diagrams.

2025-02-19: Eng review (Sanjay Rao) - Notes: Go middleware should expose context cancellation and a GetTokenBudget(ctx) helper. Also recommended default exponential backoff with jitter table in README.

notes: Trade-offs considered: a) full-featured templates vs tiny copy-paste snippets; we chose tiny labs that link to deeper docs to keep maintenance low
Streaming design: expose a small client helper `streamToRenderer` that yields chunks and an idempotency token; avoid embedding heavy state in examples
Retries: examples include a 3-tier retry matrix (fast failover for 429, capped retries for 5xx, no retries for 4xx), with language-specific wrappers
Observability: each example emits minimal structured logs (event=stream-start/stream-chunk/stream-end/retry) to simplify mapping into Console dashboards
